tip: Taw fronts a focus clause, a southern form of mai. Taw hi oedd yno stresses it was her, not someone else, who was there.
wedi marks a completed action and replaces the present-tense yn: Dw i wedi bwcio = I have booked.
unrhyw (any) triggers soft mutation: problem becomes broblem in unrhyw broblem.
Fronting the pronoun before oedd marks focus: Fe oedd wedi awgrymu = it was him, not another, who suggested it.
gyda'n gilydd means together; gilydd (each other) takes a possessive matching the group, here 'n for our.
lle links a place to a clause as where: Dyna'r pentref lle tyfais i = that's the village where I grew up.
Welsh marks possession by juxtaposing nouns, with no word for of: gwariant y llywodraeth = the government's spending.
y byddai carries reported would: Dywedodd e y byddai'n ffonio = he said that he would phone.
a (and) triggers aspirate mutation: tywyll becomes thywyll in oer a thywyll = cold and dark.
The linking yn softens a following adjective: trist becomes yn drist, da becomes yn dda.
A feminine singular noun soft-mutates after the article: gardd becomes 'r ardd = the garden.
eisoes (already) sits just before wedi: Mae hi eisoes wedi bwcio = she has already booked.
'n before a noun is short for ein (our): bwyta'n cinio = eat our lunch.
Welsh often drops the relative word that: Dyna'r mynydd dringais i = that's the mountain I climbed.
na means than after a comparative: yn hirach na'r disgwyl = longer than expected.
fod means that in reported clauses: Darllennais i fod y pris wedi codi = I read that the price had risen.
ymuno takes â (with), not a plain object: Ymunodd ein ffrindiau â ni = our friends joined us.
newydd before a verb means have just, and softens it: newydd orffen (from gorffen) = have just finished.
fy brackets the object and nasal-mutates it: dysgu becomes fy nysgu i = taught me.
The -ir ending makes an impersonal passive with no named doer: Derbynnir ceisiadau = applications are accepted.
The -af ending forms the superlative: ieuengaf = youngest, from the irregular ifanc.
For she in reported speech use ei bod hi: Dywedodd Siân ei bod hi'n mynd = Siân said she was going.
For he in reported speech use ei fod e: ei fod e'n symud = that he was moving.
cael plus a possessive forms the passive: yn cael eu hadrodd = are told, literally get their telling.
